findings.evidence: In the TM108 body the only logging call is CParam::SetTestResult at test.cpp:2304-2306, i.e. 3 of the 10 logPlan rows. INDEPENDENT CAPABILITY CHECK (the claim C11 told me to verify myself, not accept): I stripped comments from the whole copy with a string-literal-aware stripper and inventoried every callable in real code. The ONLY log-writing call anywhere in test.cpp is SetTestResult (187 code call sites; 188 raw text occurrences, the 188th being inside a comment). The only other callable whose name matches log|trace|report|print|record|output|result is GetMeasResult (64 sites, a measurement readback, not a log write) plus STSSetInitSelectDialog (2 sites, a UI dialog). 'LogData' occurs 91 times and is ALWAYS a '// ====== Step 6: LogData ======' comment header, never a call. printf/cout appear only in the hotkey/UI code at test.cpp:390 and :564-569. No function DEFINITION in test.cpp takes a string/format argument for logging. The conclusion holds for BOTH copies of treg.h in the tree. (iii) treg.h:176 TREG_ERROR::treg_error_log: technically CALLABLE (public static, and treg.h reaches test.cpp through StdAfx.h) but NOT A logPlan VEHICLE - its definition (treg.cpp:227-251) is a debug console error channel: it increments error_count and on the first call does FreeConsole(); AllocConsole(); SetConsoleTitleA(AccoTEST Debug Window); freopen(conout$, w+t, stdout); then printf_s on a numbered line built from the format. C11.detail: I take the position that 'it is in the comments' does NOT satisfy R3 s6 logPlan as a record, and I say so as a verdict rather than deferring it. R3 s6 (md :530-551) is a table of logicalIds in a section called logPlan, with a kind column that distinguishes calculated from raw context from context; its notes justify each raw-context row by what a reader of the LOG must be able to see ('without it a reviewer cannot tell which premise was in force' for triggerModeRise/Fall; 'a log that hides the geometry makes the conflict unresolvable after the fact' for sweepGeometry; 'the applied values must be logged, not the contested ones' for registerActivationTrace), and R3 md :486 requires a no-trigger segment to RECORD the failure context including 'the actual start/stop/step/interval values used' rather than write a substituted number. A static comment cannot carry 'the values actually used' - it is text that would not follow the code if the code changed. So the requirement is for emitted records. The implementation emits 3 of 10 rows (test.cpp:2304-2306) and the code concedes the rest are comments (test.cpp:2296-2299). Both branches of C11 were checked, and the second one is the one that holds: I independently verified the capability claim rather than accepting it, with a string-literal-aware comment stripper over the whole file - the only log-writing call in real code anywhere in test.cpp is SetTestResult (187 call sites), GetMeasResult is a measurement readback, LogData's 91 occurrences are all comment headers, printf/cout exist only in the UI code at :390 and :564-569, and no logging function is defined in the file; the active standard R-LOG (rules-registry.md:37) likewise defines the log rule in terms of SetTestResult and names no other primitive. I also found the same rule fails on the failure path: the code has no no-trigger detection, so a segment with no trigger would log the 0 initialiser (marked as inference RR-02, since the primitive's no-trigger behaviour is undocumented). Corroboration: the framework own logdata helper source/src/treg.cpp:62 stslogdata() itself writes through CParam::SetTestResult, and no other log-API name exists anywhere in the tree.
